rated_messages.input_message: Instead of smoking, take 10 deep, slow breaths and count them. Pay attention to what your breathing feels like. If you lose count, that's okay, just start over at 1 until you get to 10.
Notice how stress and anxiety may pull you and make you want to smoke. Just notice this. You can choose to just notice and not smoke.
Instead of lighting up a cigarette, light a scented candle or burn some incense.
Instead of smoking, use the next two minutes to pay close attention to your senses. Notice what you see, hear, feel, taste, and smell. Urges are just one part of your experience.
Crumple a piece of paper into a ball and imagine it is your urge. Toss the "urge" into the garbage or against the wall. By doing this, you are letting go of your urges.
Think of your anxious mind like a toddler throwing a tantrum. The best way to respond is to quietly watch, but not give in.
Urges to smoke usually only last a few minutes. Distract yourself by NOT thinking about giraffes, or leave the situation until it passes.
Instead of smoking, keep your fingers busy by scrolling through your phone.
A funny thing about people is that we tend to believe what we tell ourselves. So make sure that whatever else happens today, tell yourself "I can, and I will stick to not smoking!"
Tell yourself, “I am going to quit smoking soon.” Say it out loud. Say to yourself, “I am too strong to continue smoking for the rest of my life."
